newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African millers call for regional sugar deal.
newsitem.headline: S.African millers call for regional sugar deal.

text.p: South Africa's sugar millers on Wednesday called for a resumption of ties with neighbouring Swaziland and urged southern Africa to move fast towards a regional sugar trade protocol.

Don Macleod, chairman of the South African Sugar Millers' Association, told the association's annual meeting that it was necessary for the whole of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) to enter into a protocol governing future developments and trade in sugar.

The South African Sugar Association said last year it was cutting ties with Swaziland, including Swazi access to South African training and research facilities, over claims that the Swazis were dumping their cheaper sugar on the local market.
But Macleod said although the action by the neighbouring industry had exposed South Africa to the world market, it was essential that the facilities be restored.

"Neither country benefits from this stand off position and it is important that the facilities are reinstated in return for an acceptance that unfettered access for existing and future expansions in production, cannot be allowed while a distorted world market exists," he said.
He said the proposed sugar protocol within the 12-member SADC should enable regional producers to jointly grow and create a stable block of low-cost processors.

"It is very important that in the period leading to a more level playing field, producers within the region do not expand and sell their production in such a manner that it results in their fellow sugar producers being further exposed to the dump world sugar market...". --Johannesburg newsroom, +27-11 482-1003
